Owner-approved M2 deferral: parent-child object lifetime begins with Transport Ownership and Resource Lifecycle. If this object relationship is introduced earlier, the invariant must be qualified before its first use.

Owner-approved M0 foundation scope requirement. This decision establishes applicability only and does not approve normative qualification; all governing semantics must be independently demonstrated before M0 closure.
Queued-object ownership belongs to the transport resource lifecycle introduced at M2; M0 has no queue lifecycle to qualify. Qualify before first use.
Reusable buffer borrowing and reclamation belong to M2 resource ownership; M0 does not expose borrowing semantics. Qualify before first use.
Asynchronous object reference lifetime begins with M2 transport ownership; no asynchronous object interface is authorised in M0. Qualify before first use.
Event registration and ownership belong to M2 transport lifecycle; M0 has no event registration facility. Qualify before first use.
